independent_acceptance_review.summary: The three reported defects are supported on the exact supplied manuscript. The inverse-map order is corrected by an exact coordinate-swap conjugacy that preserves every relevant kick, measure, grid, norm and heat operator; the continuous-time estimate extends to Lipschitz tests with uniform constants. These two local interfaces therefore remain Minor. Remark2.3 has a genuine reversed-scale assertion, with a verified lower-radius replacement; it does not refute the principal mixing or dissipation estimates.

problem_checks.assumptions: Every even alpha>=2; torus shears and the source's arbitrary translation-kick sequence.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: For z=(1/(2 alpha^2),0), V_plus o H_plus and H_plus o V_plus have horizontal coordinates differing by1/2. WithS(x,y)=(y,x), T_actual=S T_printed S exactly. Conjugation sends each kickxi toSxi, preserves the dyadic grid and Lebesgue measure, is isometric on every Lp, and commutes with isotropic heat. The continuous flow is transferred by the same coordinate swap.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: All main-estimate hypotheses and constants transfer by an exact symmetry; no additional dynamical estimate is missing.
problem_checks.repair: Verified exact conjugacy, with the corrected composition recorded rather than asserting literal equality.

problem_checks.independent_derivation: The dyadic-cell averages of sin(2 pi 2^m x) vanish at the stated mesh, whereas ball averages near a maximum tend to1 as radius tends to0. Thus an upper-radius condition cannot imply every smaller-radius geometric bound. Forr>=4 sqrt2 h, fully contained cells occupy at least(3/4)^2 of a ball and give the stated(1+kappa_prime)/2 bound; the torus-scale case uses mean zero.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The false scale conversion is auxiliary and does not enter the principal PDE proof with that quantifier.
problem_checks.repair: Verified the lower-radius replacement and its constants at the level claimed.

problem_checks.independent_derivation: For0<s<1/2 andg=sin(2 pi y), g o phi_s has opposite nonzero one-sided x derivatives atx=1/2,y=0 and is notC1. Periodic mollification converges uniformly and bounds its C1 norm by supnorm plus Lipschitz constant. Passing to the limit in the existing correlation estimate at fixedn preserves its constant; the flow's uniform Lipschitz bound fors in[0,1] supplies the continuous-time estimate.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: This is a bounded extension of the already proved estimate, with no extra regularity assumption or new mixing bound.
problem_checks.repair: Verified uniform Lipschitz approximation and retention of the same decay rate.

scope_and_limitations: Acceptance rechecks the reported findings, their repairs and their downstream scope; it is not a new exhaustive independent proof of every dynamical estimate.
The geometric-mixing counterexample targets the assertion for all sufficiently small radii, not the analytic-mixing theorem.
Minor grading of F1 and F3 rests on exact covariance and a norm-bounded extension of an existing estimate, not merely on the possibility of repairing a theorem.
